title: TNH April 2024 Class MSN 106 Gastrointestinal Disorders Block One Supplementary Examination

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs and True/False statements from TNH April 2024 Class MSN 106 Gastrointestinal Disorders Block One Supplementary Examination paper (sat 20 December 2024, Section A, Q1 to Q30).

questions.text: In liver disease:
questions.explanation: Ammonia levels rise (C) is correct because the damaged liver cannot convert ammonia to urea. Albumin is increased (A) is incorrect because albumin falls. Prothrombin time (INR) is normal (B) is incorrect because clotting factors fall and the INR is prolonged. Cholesterol is increased (D) is incorrect because it is usually low in liver failure.

questions.text: Regarding gastrointestinal regulatory substances:

options.B: Norepinephrine has inhibitory effect on GIT
options.D: Gastrin decreases secretion of gastric acid

questions.explanation: Histamine increases gastric acid production (C) is correct because histamine acts on H2 receptors of the parietal cells to stimulate acid secretion. Acetylcholine (A) increases acid secretion. Gastrin (D) stimulates acid secretion. Norepinephrine has inhibitory effect on GIT (B) is incorrect as the best answer because, although sympathetic activity slows the gut, the answer expected is C. Note: option B is also physiologically true, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: When a nurse is performing physical assessment for a patient with gastrointestinal disorders:

options.A: Ensures bladder is full and abdomen fully exposed
options.B: Patient lies in supine with knees slightly flexed
options.C: Percussion precedes auscultation on abdominal assessment
options.D: Knows hyperactive bowel sounds are one to two sounds in two minutes

questions.explanation: Patient lies in supine with knees slightly flexed (B) is correct because this position relaxes the abdominal muscles. Ensures bladder is full (A) is incorrect because the patient empties the bladder first. Percussion precedes auscultation (C) is incorrect because the order is inspection, auscultation, percussion and palpation. Hyperactive sounds are one to two sounds in two minutes (D) is incorrect because that describes hypoactive sounds.

questions.text: In oesophageal cancer:

options.A: Squamous cell carcinoma accounts for most of cancer of oesophagus
options.B: Squamous cell carcinoma arises from the lower portion of oesophagus
options.C: Adenocarcinoma arise from the surface epithelium
options.D: Females are at a higher risk of developing oesophageal cancer

questions.explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma accounts for most of cancer of oesophagus (A) is correct because it is the most common type worldwide and in Africa. Option B is incorrect because squamous cell cancer is mostly in the middle esophagus and adenocarcinoma in the lower. Option C is incorrect because adenocarcinoma arises from glandular (Barrett's) epithelium. Option D is incorrect because men are at higher risk.

questions.text: In care for a patient post esophagectomy:

options.A: Advocate for chest physiotherapy to avoid aspiration
options.B: Perform a barium swallow before patient is allowed to feed
options.C: Patient should be allowed to sleep in prone position
options.D: Manipulate the nasogastric tube to check the anastomotic area

questions.explanation: Advocate for chest physiotherapy to avoid aspiration (A) is correct because the patient has a thoracic or abdominal incision and is at risk of atelectasis and aspiration pneumonia, so deep breathing, coughing and chest physiotherapy are done with the head of the bed raised. Prone position (C) is incorrect because the patient is kept semi-upright. Manipulate the nasogastric tube (D) is incorrect because the tube must not be moved or reinserted, as it can damage the anastomosis. Barium swallow before feeding (B) is incorrect as the best answer, although a contrast study is done later to check for leaks. Note: option B is used in some protocols, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Medication used for achalasia of cardia management includes:
questions.explanation: Calcium channel blockers (B) is correct because drugs such as nifedipine relax the smooth muscle of the lower esophageal sphincter. NSAIDs (A), anticoagulants (C) and antibiotics (D) are incorrect because they do not relax the sphincter.

questions.text: The recommended diet for a patient with liver cirrhosis is:
questions.explanation: High carbohydrates (D) is correct because carbohydrates give energy and spare protein, and the usual diet is high in calories and carbohydrate with moderate protein. High proteins (A) is incorrect because protein is restricted when there is encephalopathy. High fat (B) is incorrect because fat is limited with poor bile flow. Low fiber (C) is incorrect because fibre helps prevent constipation and ammonia absorption.

questions.text: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome is associated with:
questions.explanation: Hyperchlorhydria (A) is correct because the gastrin-secreting tumour causes excessive gastric acid. Achlorhydria (B) is incorrect because it means no acid. Diabetes mellitus (C) and excess mucus secretion (D) are not features.

questions.text: A potential complication of chronic pancreatitis is:
questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus (C) is correct because chronic inflammation destroys the islet cells, so insulin production falls. Gastric ulcers (A), cholecystitis (B) and hypothyroidism (D) are not typical complications.

questions.text: A haemorrhoid characterized by prolapse on defecation requiring manual reduction is:
questions.explanation: Third degree (C) is correct because these prolapse on straining and must be pushed back by hand. First degree (A) does not prolapse, second degree (B) reduces spontaneously and fourth degree (D) is permanently prolapsed.

questions.text: Calculous cholecystitis is caused by:

options.A: Obstruction of bile flow by bile stones
options.B: Inflammation in absence of bile stones

questions.explanation: Obstruction of bile flow by bile stones (A) is correct because a stone blocking the cystic duct traps bile, which causes inflammation. Inflammation in absence of stones (B) describes acalculous cholecystitis. Lack of gall bladder contraction (C) and reduced bile viscosity (D) are not the cause.

questions.text: A medication used to manage ascites by increasing renal sodium excretion is:
questions.explanation: Furosemide (A) is correct because this loop diuretic increases the excretion of sodium and water by the kidney (often with spironolactone). Mannitol (B) is an osmotic diuretic for cerebral edema, albumin (C) raises oncotic pressure and lactulose (D) is a laxative.

questions.text: In management of hepatic encephalitis, the drug of choice is:
questions.explanation: Lactulose (A) is correct because it acidifies the colon, traps ammonia as ammonium, and speeds its removal. Lasix (B), bisacodyl (C) and dexamethasone (D) do not lower ammonia.

questions.text: The major cause of peptic ulcers is:
questions.explanation: Helicobacter pylori (A) is correct because this bacterium is found in most duodenal ulcers and many gastric ulcers; NSAIDs are the second main cause. Alcohol, smoking and spicy foods are contributing factors but not the main cause.

questions.text: The appropriate health messages for a patient with colostomy on discharge is to:

options.D: Report dark colour change in stoma

questions.explanation: Report dark colour change in stoma (D) is correct because a dark, purple or black stoma shows poor blood supply (ischemia) and needs urgent review. Eggs and garlic (A) cause odour and gas. Sugary food (B) causes gas and diarrhoea. Increasing water with meals (C) is not advised as a measure.

questions.text: The modifiable risk factor for colon cancer is:
questions.explanation: Obesity (D) is correct because weight can be changed. Age, genetics and family history cannot be modified.

questions.text: Diverticulosis commonly affects:
questions.explanation: Sigmoid colon (D) is correct because the sigmoid has the narrowest lumen and the highest pressure, so most diverticula form there.

questions.text: The classical symptom of appendicitis is:
questions.explanation: Right lower quadrant pain (B) is correct because the pain moves from the umbilicus to McBurney's point as the peritoneum becomes inflamed. Umbilical pain (D) and epigastric pain (C) are early and vague, and left lower quadrant pain (A) suggests diverticulitis.

questions.text: In management of appendicitis:

options.A: Patient is encouraged to take high fibre diet
options.B: A nasogastric tube is inserted to facilitate feeding
options.C: Laxatives are given in case of constipation
options.D: Patient is maintained nil by mouth

questions.explanation: Patient is maintained nil by mouth (D) is correct because the patient may need emergency surgery, and food could cause vomiting and aspiration. Fibre (A), feeding by nasogastric tube (B) and laxatives (C) are incorrect because laxatives and food can cause rupture.

questions.text: Pre-hepatic cause of portal hypertension includes:
questions.explanation: Portal vein thrombosis (A) is correct because the block is before the liver. Hepatic vein thrombosis (B) and right sided heart failure (C) are post-hepatic, and liver cirrhosis (D) is intrahepatic.

questions.text: Mechanical cause of intestinal obstruction include:
questions.explanation: Faecal impaction (D) is correct because hard stool physically blocks the lumen. Paralytic ileus (A), Hirschsprung's disease (B) and muscular dystrophy (C) are functional (neurogenic or muscular) causes where there is no physical block.

questions.text: Management of dumping syndrome include:

options.B: Taking food while in a low fowler's position
options.C: Sitting upright for 20 minutes after food intake

questions.explanation: Reduced fluid intake with food (A) is correct because fluid with meals speeds emptying, so fluids are taken between meals. Low Fowler's position (B) is incorrect because the patient should lie down after meals to slow emptying. Sitting upright for 20 minutes (C) is incorrect because it does the opposite. More carbohydrates than proteins (D) is incorrect because the diet is high in protein and low in simple carbohydrate.

questions.text: Ileostomy effluent:
questions.explanation: Is mushy liquid stool (A) is correct because the ileum discharges liquid to pasty content as the colon is bypassed. Absence of digestive enzymes (B) is incorrect because the effluent contains enzymes that irritate the skin. Low in pH (C) is incorrect because the effluent is alkaline. Output is highly predictable (D) is incorrect because the output is continuous and unpredictable.

questions.text: The risk factor for gallstones developments is:
questions.explanation: Obesity (B) is correct because it increases cholesterol secretion into bile. Low cholesterol (A), high-fibre diet (C) and regular exercise (D) are protective.

questions.text: A sign of complete intestinal obstruction is:
questions.explanation: Absence of bowel sounds (D) is correct because in complete obstruction the bowel becomes silent. Passage of flatus (A) is incorrect because nothing passes. Hyperactive sounds (C) occur early in partial obstruction. Hypoactive sounds (B) are incorrect as the best answer because complete obstruction gives absent sounds.

questions.text: Murphy's sign is a physical examination finding associated with:
questions.explanation: Cholecystitis (B) is correct because the inflamed gallbladder causes pain and halts inspiration when the right subcostal area is pressed. It is not a sign of appendicitis (A), cholelithiasis (C) or pancreatitis (D).

questions.text: A complication of gastric resection is:
questions.explanation: Dumping syndrome (B) is correct because after resection the contents of the stomach empty too quickly into the small bowel. The other options are not typical complications.

questions.text: The priority focus of nursing management for a client with peritonitis is:
questions.explanation: Fluid and electrolyte balance (A) is correct because large amounts of fluid shift into the peritoneal cavity and bowel, which causes hypovolemic shock. Pain management (C) is important but is not the first priority, gastric irrigation (B) is not routine and psychosocial issues (D) come later.

questions.text: When a segment of intestine slides into an adjacent part of the intestine is called:
questions.explanation: Intussusception (B) is correct because one segment of bowel telescopes into the next. Volvulus (A) is twisting, hernia (C) is protrusion through the abdominal wall and adhesions (D) are fibrous bands.

questions.text: A common cause of gastritis is:
questions.explanation: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (D) is correct because NSAIDs block prostaglandins and damage the protective mucosa. Milk (A) and bicarbonate of soda (B) are not causes. Enteric coated aspirin (C) is incorrect as the best answer because it is itself an NSAID with less gastric irritation. Note: option C is also plausible, so check this item against the marking scheme.
